summary: Backend regression suite covering KasirKu Pro: auth (register/login/me/duplicate/unauthorized), products CRUD (incl. kitchen_print, cost, min_stock, 404 edge cases), transactions (sale cash reduces stock & reflects in reports, purchase increases stock, sale_return restores stock, insufficient cash & stock rejected with 400, credit sale creates receivable, /pay reduces outstanding and auto-logs cash entry, filter by kind, detail 404), debts (receivable+payable aggregation), cash entries (income/expense CRUD), operators (create/list/update/delete, permission enforcement - cashier blocked from POST /api/products with 403), permissions preset endpoint, reports summary (daily/monthly/yearly with all required fields), settings (default + update with 80mm & logo_base64, business_name propagates), backup (products/transactions/cash_entries present), integrations status (qris/whatsapp/bluetooth_printing all unconfigured). Result: 32/32 passed (100%). No ObjectId (_id) leaks detected in any response. One minor backend design issue noted: OperatorInput requires password (min_length=6) on PUT, even though logic only updates when non-empty - clients cannot easily 'edit without changing password'.

minor.issue: OperatorInput.password is required with min_length=6, so clients cannot send an empty password to keep the existing one. Backend already contains the logic 'if payload.password and payload.password.strip()' suggesting it was intended optional. Suggest making password Optional[str] in OperatorInput (or defining a separate OperatorUpdateInput) so edit-without-password works.

action_items: Make OperatorInput.password Optional[str] (or create OperatorUpdateInput) so PUT /api/operators/{id} can keep existing password without client sending a 6+ char dummy value.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py (604 lines) is nearing the 700-line soft limit; consider splitting into routers (auth, products, transactions, cash, operators, reports, settings) for maintainability.
DELETE /api/products first sets deleted_at then hard-deletes immediately - the soft-delete marker never persists. Either keep soft-delete (and filter deleted in queries) or drop the two-step dance.
report_summary filters by created_at string ISO - works because ISO is lexicographically ordered in UTC, but assumes no mixed timezones. Fine today, worth flagging.
No rate limiting or lockout on /api/auth/login - acceptable for MVP but worth adding later.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run registers a fresh owner with username test_<uuid> and creates a scoped cashier operator; all created products/customers/categories/entries are TEST_ prefixed for identification. No seeded data was modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use EXPO_BACKEND_URL=EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (preview URL). Run `pytest backend/tests/test_backend_full.py -v`. Fixtures (owner, cashier) are module-scoped; parallel pytest-xdist is OK. The test_update_operator test sends a 6+ char password string because OperatorInput mandates it - adjust once backend makes password Optional. Mocked integrations: QRIS, WhatsApp Cloud API, Bluetooth printing all report configured=false by design.
rca_of_issue: Initial failure test_update_operator (422) root cause: OperatorInput.password has min_length=6, so sending password='' violates Pydantic validation before reaching the 'keep old password' branch in backend code. Fix at test level by passing a valid password string; actual backend fix should make password Optional[str] in the Pydantic model so the existing 'if payload.password and payload.password.strip():' guard behaves as intended.
